content.value_statement: Crypto market data work is hard when exchanges use different feeds and formats. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Cryptofeed setup, callbacks, channels, and backend choices.
actual_capabilities: Explains FeedHandler setup for single and multi-exchange streams.
Shows how to subscribe to ticker, trade, order book, and NBBO data.
Summarizes supported exchanges, public channels, private channels, and storage backends.
Guides callback design for streaming market data workflows.
Points to reference documentation for REST interfaces and installation choices.
limitations: It does not provide live market data by itself.
It does not manage exchange API keys or trading account security.
It cannot verify current exchange support without checking upstream documentation.
It offers guidance only; users must test code against target exchanges.

use_cases.title: Stream Multi-Exchange Prices
use_cases.description: Plan ticker and trade subscriptions across exchanges with normalized callbacks and clear symbol handling.

use_cases.title: Analyze Order Book Depth
use_cases.description: Design L2 book subscriptions and callback flows for depth monitoring, spread checks, and liquidity research.

use_cases.title: Choose Market Data Storage
use_cases.description: Compare backend options for writing normalized market events to queues, databases, or time-series stores.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up First Feed
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for one exchange and one symbol.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up a basic Cryptofeed stream for one exchange and one symbol. Explain imports, callbacks, channel choice, and run steps.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Exchange Channels
prompt_templates.prompt: I need BTC and ETH market data from several exchanges. Recommend Cryptofeed channels and explain tradeoffs for ticker, trades, and order book updates.

prompt_templates.title: Design Backend Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Cryptofeed pipeline that writes normalized trade and L2 book data to a backend. Include callback responsibilities, storage options, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my proposed Cryptofeed architecture for multi-exchange NBBO monitoring, private channel separation, reconnection behavior, and operational risks. Highlight gaps and testing needs.

output_examples.input: I want Coinbase BTC-USD ticker updates.
output_examples.output: Start with FeedHandler, choose Coinbase, subscribe to the ticker channel, and create a callback that records each normalized ticker event.

output_examples.input: I need order book data from Binance and Kraken.
output: Use L2 book channels when aggregated depth is enough.
Check symbol naming for each exchange before subscribing.
Plan storage and backpressure before increasing symbol count.

output_examples.input: Which backend should I use for market data history?
output_examples.output: Use Kafka or RabbitMQ for streaming pipelines, Redis for fast recent data, and a database when historical querying matters.

best_practices: Start with public channels before adding authenticated account channels.
Use a virtual environment and install only optional backends you need.
Test symbol names and channel support per exchange before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every exchange supports the same channels or symbol formats.
Do not print sensitive private channel data in logs.
Do not connect many high-volume feeds without backpressure and storage planning.

faq.question: Does this skill fetch live market data?
faq.answer: No. It explains how to use Cryptofeed. The installed library connects to exchanges when you run your own code.

faq.question: Which AI tools support it?
faq.answer: The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it help with private exchange channels?
faq.answer: Yes. It can explain authenticated channels such as balances, fills, order status, and transactions. You must protect API credentials.

faq.question: Does it place trades?
faq.answer: It can explain related REST concepts when documented. It is not a trading bot and requires exchange safeguards.

faq.question: Can it store market data?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes backend choices such as Redis, Kafka, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, and time-series databases.

faq.question: Is exchange support always current?
faq.answer: No. Exchange APIs change. Check upstream Cryptofeed documentation before relying on production compatibility.
